exposure: Reasons for ICU admission (obstetric vs. non-obstetric factors)
outcome: Pregnancy outcomes (cesarean section rate, pregnancy termination, induced abortion)
cohort: The study participants were 152 critically ill pregnant women admitted to the Intensive Care Unit.
finding: Non-obstetric factors were the primary contributors for ICU admission and were associated with a higher maternal mortality rate compared to obstetric factors, while higher SOFA scores also indicated increased mortality.
mod_finding: The cesarean section rate was significantly higher in the group admitted to the ICU due to obstetric factors compared to those admitted due to non-obstetric factors.
